analysis:
The PR adds one opt-in live test, provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Live/PrefixQualification/ModelCheckpointConversationLiveTests.swift (head lines 1-192). It is gated by DARKBLOOM_CHECKPOINT_CONVERSATION_BENCHMARK=1 and requires an absolute, not-yet-existing output path and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_EXCLUSIVE_GPU=1. The test file adds no production code, endpoint, protocol, key handling or deployment change.

The prompts are public synthetic text ("Record N: station ..."), not consumer data (A-001). The JSON report (lines 39-52, written atomically) holds only model ID, weight hash, timings, token counts, file and byte counts, and failure strings. It contains no prompts, keys or tokens. The output path comes from a developer-set environment variable and is checked for absoluteness and non-existence, but the check is not symlink-hardened. That is a local test-harness matter, not a production boundary.

The test exercises prefix-cache (T-041) behavior: restored tokens, stage-cap disposition and bytes written per turn. It records TTFT and prefix-restore observations. With a synthetic public prompt, that is an observation rather than a new oracle. It does not change the TTL, the HMAC lookup names, salt scoping, the disk budget or the KEK handling. It uses SPI/@testable access to internal types (ModelPrefixBenchmarkFixture, EngineV2Factory.benchmarkPrompt, session.cacheSnapshot and drainCheckpointWrites); I did not see these definitions. Because the test requires native live and checkpoint quantization and excludes mimo_v2, it avoids lossy profiles.

Residual questions for later passes: the `@_spi(Benchmarking)` surfaces it uses must not be reachable from production builds, and the benchmark fixture must not weaken real cache scoping or the storage validation in CacheVolume. Neither can be checked from the supplied evidence. No security regression identified.
